anatomy.flutter: UserMenu builds SidebarMenu > SidebarMenuItem > DropdownMenu whose trigger is SidebarMenuButton(child: SidebarMenuRow(leading: Avatar, label: _IdentityText, trailing: Icon.lucide(chevronsUpDown))), and whose children are rows built from _identity() (Avatar + _IdentityText) plus MenuLabel/MenuGroup/MenuItem/MenuSeparator, per user_menu.dart lines 109-166.
anatomy.web: UserMenu renders SidebarMenu > SidebarMenuItem > DropdownMenu > DropdownMenuTrigger(SidebarMenuButton(Identity + ChevronsUpDown Icon)) and DropdownMenuContent(DropdownMenuLabel(Identity), DropdownMenuGroup of DropdownMenuItem, destructive DropdownMenuItem group), per components/ui/user-menu.tsx lines 144-227 — the same slot list: trigger row, repeated identity header, normal group, separator, destructive group.

api.flutter: UserMenu({required UserMenuAccount user, required List<UserMenuItem> items}); UserMenuAccount(name, email, avatar: ImageProvider?); UserMenuItem(label, icon: LucideGlyph?, onSelect: VoidCallback?, destructive = false) — user_menu.dart lines 44-84, 87-92, both required with no default list.

states.flutter: SidebarMenuButton inherits the sidebar's own rest/hover/focus/active states (SidebarMenuButton in sidebar.dart), and the menu itself opens/closes via DropdownMenu — there is no loading/success/error/disabled state modeled anywhere in user_menu.dart, matching a synchronous disclosure with no request in flight.
states.web: The doc page's States section explicitly limits itself to closed / trigger focus-visible / empty items (components/docs/component-docs/user-menu/page.tsx lines 179-199) and states 'Sizes and Variants are omitted... loading, success and error are N/A... disabled is N/A' (lines 204-225) because opening is synchronous and there is no whole-control disable prop.

disabled.flutter: UserMenu, UserMenuAccount and UserMenuItem carry no disabled field anywhere in user_menu.dart — there is no whole-control or per-item disable path to model.
disabled.web: UserMenuItem has no disabled field either (components/ui/user-menu.tsx lines 24-38), and the doc page states this explicitly: 'disabled is N/A: there is no prop to disable the whole control, and disabling one item is a property of the caller's own onSelect' (components/docs/component-docs/user-menu/page.tsx lines 220-224).
disabled.note: Both sides agree there is no disabled state for this component by design, so n/a is the correct verdict rather than gap — this is not an unmodeled state, it is a deliberately absent one on both platforms.

interaction.flutter: mobile in user_menu.dart line 100 is read only as `scope?.isMobile ?? false`, and side is chosen with `mobile ? PopoverSide.bottom : PopoverSide.right` (line 141) — there is no second, narrower breakpoint check anywhere in the file, so DropdownMenu's dismissal/placement behaviour is driven off one boolean.
interaction.web: components/ui/user-menu.tsx lines 41-77 implement a dedicated useIsNarrow() hook at max-width: 1023px specifically because isMobile alone is false at exactly 768px, where the sidebar row is full-width and side="right" measured 694px wide starting 33px outside the viewport (lines 45-63, 160-183) — a real, photographed defect the web side fixed by adding a second query so the menu still opens somewhere the pointer can reach it.
interaction.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: This is a genuine, documented parity gap: the Flutter UserMenu's placement logic (mobile ? bottom : right) reproduces the exact off-screen-menu bug the web side's own code comments describe finding and fixing at the 768-1023px tablet band, because it has no equivalent of useIsNarrow's max-width:1023px query. A Flutter build at a tablet-width viewport with the sidebar expanded will very likely open this menu off-screen the same way the pre-fix web build did, making the dropdown unreachable by pointer or touch. File: lib/src/components/ui/user_menu.dart, line 100 (`final bool mobile = scope?.isMobile ?? false;`) and line 141 (`side: mobile ? PopoverSide.bottom : PopoverSide.right`).
